title: pipes_between can return a count larger than the caller's buffer; compute_route then slices pair_buf[:cnt] out of bounds
detail: n increments past len(out); pair_buf is [MAX_ROUTE]u32 (32). More than 32 parallel pipes between one pair panics the slice. Prevented only by catalog port capacities, which the loader never enforces for junctions (port_capacity 0 validates fine).
recommended_fix: Clamp the return to len(out) in pipes_between, or reject cnt > MAX_ROUTE before slicing; validate junction port_capacity > 0 at load.

title: Paths longer than MAX_ROUTE silently become 'unreachable' — the packet/demand drops though a route exists
detail: A reachable destination beyond 32 pipes reports route_len=0, indistinguishable from genuinely unroutable; E28 accrual and the Unreachable drop reason then misattribute the loss. Out of PROTO scale, but silent.
recommended_fix: Assert topology/path bounds at load or use a distinct drop reason for route-overflow.

title: Severance reroute resets edge_idx/progress_units but not vis_q8 — the visual fraction can overrun the new route
evidence:
+		cur := current_node(p, t)
+		compute_route(f, t, cur, p.dst, p)
+		p.edge_idx = 0
+		p.progress_units = 0
detail: vis_q8 (T1-hashed, deterministic) is unchanged; on a shorter new route packet_edge_pos falls through to 'return 0, 0, p.dst', rendering the packet at its destination. Cosmetic, but a visible teleport after reroute.
recommended_fix: Reset or rescale vis_q8 when a reroute replaces the route.

title: Cmd_Set_Pipe_Priority / Cmd_Set_Junction_Triage accept any negative value below -1
detail: No lower bound: -2..min(i32) pass validation, are stored and serialized as distinct states, yet behave as neutral (-1). Two byte-different encodings of 'neutral' diverge the hash for identical behavior.
recommended_fix: Reject priority/triage < -1 in validate_command (and in log replay).

title: Set-piece fields unvalidated: duration_ticks 0 never activates; forecast_lead_ticks > start_tick never forecasts
evidence:
+				sp.duration_ticks = u64(jint(so, "duration_ticks", 0))
+				sp.forecast_lead_ticks = u64(jint(so, "forecast_lead_ticks", 0))
... (catalog.odin set-piece guard) ...
+	return sp.forecast_lead_ticks <= sp.start_tick &&
+	       tick >= sp.start_tick - sp.forecast_lead_ticks && tick < sp.start_tick
detail: The lead guard silently never fires on a misconfigured lead time; a zero-duration surge never triggers and never resolves. ODN-5 fail-fast validation does not cover these fields.
recommended_fix: Validate duration_ticks >= 1 and forecast_lead_ticks <= start_tick at catalog load.

title: Hysteresis band drains 1/tick even at zero/negative severity (uptime at/above the win threshold)
evidence:
+			severity := bal.win_uptime_pct - recent_uptime
+			drain := clamp(severity / 10, 1, bal.meter_drain_per_tick_max) // E16
detail: Inside an open episode, uptime between win_uptime_pct (90) and breach_exit_pct (93) keeps in_breach true with severity <= 0; the clamp floor forces a 1/tick drain while uptime is at/above the win bar. Undocumented if intended.
recommended_fix: Gate the drain on recent_uptime < win_uptime_pct, or document the deliberate band bleed.

title: jint silently truncates fractional JSON numbers in integer catalog fields
detail: With parse_integers=true a Float appears only from a non-integer literal (e.g. 1.9); it truncates to 1 instead of failing. ODN-5 promises fail-fast on bad values; wrong-type values slip through truncated.
recommended_fix: Reject json.Float in integer fields (fail-fast), or round-trip check i32(x) == x.

title: Overlapping set pieces: surge_active goes false while a later surge is still active; surge_ends_in is last-wins
detail: A single boolean and a single countdown serve a list of set pieces; two overlapping surges leave the run 'not in surge' during the second. The PROTO catalog has one surge, so latent — the schema permits more.
recommended_fix: Compute surge_active/surge_ends_in from the currently-active set-piece set.
